about.title: Adelanto Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Adelanto's growth along corridors like Palmdale Road and Bellflower Street has brought more retail centers, warehouses, and apartment properties into daily life — and with that comes more opportunities for wet floors, broken pavement, poor lighting, and neglected stairwells. When a property owner fails to catch and fix a hazard they knew about (or should have known about), California law allows an injured person to pursue compensation. These cases hinge on evidence: photos of the hazard, witness names, and surveillance footage that many businesses only keep for a short time. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise any result — we simply connect Adelanto residents hurt in a fall with an independent attorney who can evaluate the property owner's responsibility, gather the evidence before it disappears, and explain your options under a contingency arrangement, meaning there's no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Property Owner's Insurer

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires showing the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it. An attorney can help identify maintenance logs, prior complaints, or repair history that establish that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Adelanto businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to send a preservation letter can be the difference between having proof and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you're partly blamed for not seeing a hazard, California's pure comparative fault rule still lets you recover a percentage of damages — an attorney can help push back against unfair fault allocations.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Adelanto?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall under California law, though claims against a government-owned property (like a public sidewalk) have a much shorter window. Because of that shorter deadline for public entities, it's worth speaking with an attorney soon after a fall on any city or county property. Waiting too long can permanently bar your claim regardless of how strong the evidence is.

items.question: What if the store or apartment complex says they didn't know about the hazard?
items.answer: That's actually the central issue in most premises liability cases — proving the owner knew or should have known. Evidence like prior complaints, how long a spill or crack had existed, or a lack of routine inspections can help establish notice. An independent attorney can help gather and interpret this evidence.

items.question: Does Adelanto's growth and traffic near Rt 395 and Palmdale Road affect fall accidents?
items.answer: Not directly, but the same growth that's increased crash reports along those corridors has also brought more commercial properties, parking lots, and foot traffic into Adelanto. More properties and more visitors can mean more opportunities for unaddressed hazards, which is part of why documenting conditions after a fall matters.
